title: Conditional Sentences
explanation: Conditionals express hypothetical situations and their consequences. Zero: general truths (If + present, present). First: real future possibilities (If + present, will + verb). Second: unreal present/future (If + past simple, would + verb). Third: unreal past (If + past perfect, would have + past participle).
examples: Zero: If you heat water to 100°C, it boils. (always true)
First: If it rains tomorrow, I will stay home. (real possibility)
Second: If I won the lottery, I would travel the world. (unreal/hypothetical)
Third: If I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam. (unreal past)

exercises.question: If I ___ (be) you, I would accept the offer.
exercises.explanation: Second conditional: If + past simple. 'Were' is used for all persons in formal English.

exercises.question: If she ___ (study) more, she would have passed.
If it ___ (rain), we will cancel the picnic.
If you mix red and blue, you ___ (get) purple.
exercises.explanation: Zero conditional: If + present, present. General truth.

exercises.question: I ___ (travel) the world if I had more money.
exercises.explanation: Second conditional: would + verb for hypothetical present/future.
